sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Ili Turki language' (en) and 土尔克语 (zh), plus tr/ru/de/ja/fr editions (read online 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Consonant and vowel inventories only (zh cites Zhao & Aximu 1985 pp. 27-28); no stress/accent statement in any edition. Used only to harvest bibliography (adds 程试、胡毅 1990 语言与翻译 1990(2): 20-22 and 新疆民族语言分布状况与发展趋势 2002 pp. 338-346).

sources.citation: Johanson, Lars 2001. Discoveries on the Turkic Linguistic Map. Stockholm: Svenska Forskningsinstitutet i Istanbul (PDF at turkoloji.cu.edu.tr).
sources.note: Does not treat Ili Turki at all (German Wikipedia's attribution is wrong); nothing on stress. Not.

sources.citation: Hahn, Reinhard F. 1991. An Annotated Sample of Ili Turki. Acta Orientalia Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 45(1): 31-53.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 1 'Phonology' (pp. 33-34) covers vowel neutralization, raising/reduction ('Any vowel in a "light" non-initial open syllable is reduced to [ə]'), devoicing, aspiration, l-velarization, fricativization, final devoicing and harmony; sections 2-3 are morphology and a comparative lexical list. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0).

sources.note: The principal English-language linguistic outline of Ili Turki (phoneme inventory, morphophonology, classification); the most likely Western-language source for an explicit word-stress statement. Named by our earlier survey as the unreachable source.
